headline: Protocol contract-code upgrades (T1, can replace any registered contract incl. rETH/deposit logic) are held by a 10-member Oracle DAO whose Security-Council qualification and on-chain upgrade timelock could not be verified this run.
short_headline: oDAO holds T1 upgrades; timelock unverified

findings.text: Rocket Pool uses a registry-pointer upgrade pattern, not proxies: RocketStorage (0x1d8f...) stores every contract address via setAddress(bytes32,address); getDeployedStatus()=true. Replacing a registered address swaps the live implementation of fund-holding contracts, so the upgrade surface is T1 fund-critical.

RocketDAONodeTrustedUpgrade (0x9290...) exposes upgrade(string,string,string,address) and bootstrapUpgrade(...) write methods that (per its ContractUpgraded/ContractAdded events and role) write RocketStorage.setAddress, giving it authority over all registered contracts. It is gated to the Oracle DAO, not an EOA.

RocketDAONodeTrusted (0xb8e7...) reports getMemberCount()=10, getMemberMinRequired()=3, getMemberQuorumVotesRequired()=5100000000000000000 (51%), and getBootstrapModeDisabled()=true. The oDAO is the body that authorizes upgrades; it is a 10-member trusted-node set, not a 2-of-3 or single EOA.

RocketStorage.getGuardian()=0x0cCF14983364A7735d369879603930Afe10df21e. With getDeployedStatus()=true and the oDAO's bootstrap mode disabled, the guardian's bootstrap shortcut functions are no longer usable; no direct guardian storage-write path was confirmable on-chain this run.

Highest reachable tier on the upgrade path is T1: upgrade()/addContract() can replace the implementation address of any fund-holding contract (rETH, deposit pool, minipool logic) via RocketStorage.setAddress. The binding functions are upgrade(...) on 0x9290... and setAddress(bytes32,address) on RocketStorage.

Uncontested fast-path delay for an oDAO contract-upgrade proposal (asserted 7d vote-delay + 14d vote + 28d execute window on settings contract 0xAD038f...) could not be independently re-read on-chain this run; the read API returned network errors for that non-surfacer address and the surfacer URL was not allowlisted.

steelman.red: The contract-code upgrade authority can replace any fund-holding contract (T1) via RocketStorage.setAddress, an unbounded power over user funds.
steelman.orange: That T1 upgrade power is held by a 10-member Oracle DAO that fails or is unverified against the Security-Council test (non-insider signer share and timelock not confirmable on-chain this run), placing a not-clearly-qualified body on a T1 path.
steelman.green: Bootstrap mode is disabled so no guardian EOA shortcut exists, upgrades require a ≥51% quorum of a 10-member oDAO with a long documented multi-week vote+execute window providing an exit notice period.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because the green steel-man depends on two facts I could not verify on-chain this run — that the oDAO meets the Security-Council standard (≥50% publicly-announced non-insider signers) and that the upgrade fast path carries a ≥7-day timelock — while the on-chain reads I did obtain confirm a genuine T1 upgrade surface (RocketStorage.setAddress reachable via RocketDAONodeTrustedUpgrade.upgrade) held by a 10-member body. A T1 path held by a multisig-like body that is not confirmed to satisfy Security-Council criteria maps to orange, not green; it is not red because the authority is a 10-member 51%-quorum DAO with bootstrap shortcuts disabled, not a single EOA or 2-of-3.

evidence.shows: RocketDAONodeTrustedUpgrade ABI: write methods upgrade(string,string,string,address), bootstrapUpgrade(...), addContract via ContractAdded/ContractUpgraded events; veto/execute proposal flow. Demonstrates this contract holds protocol contract-upgrade authority (derived: it writes RocketStorage.setAddress per its role and events).

RocketStorage live reads: getDeployedStatus()=true, getGuardian()=0x0cCF14983364A7735d369879603930Afe10df21e; write surface setAddress(bytes32,address) is the registry pointer that defines every contract's live implementation address.

RocketDAONodeTrusted live reads pinned to block 25246395: getMemberCount()=10, getMemberMinRequired()=3, getMemberQuorumVotesRequired()=5100000000000000000 (51%), getBootstrapModeDisabled()=true. Establishes the Oracle DAO membership/quorum authorizing upgrades and that bootstrap shortcuts are disabled.

unknowns: C3: oDAO contract-upgrade fast-path delay (asserted 7d vote-delay + 14d vote + 28d execute on rocketDAONodeTrustedSettingsProposals 0xAD038f8994a6bd51C8A72D3721CEd83401D4d2b0) not re-read on-chain in this run; settings address is not an allowlisted surfacer and direct /api/contract/read calls returned network errors — corroboration only.
C3-offchain: numeric upgrade-timelock constants taken from address_book prose were not re-read on-chain this run; value not re-verified, corroboration only.

C4: signer identities of the 10 oDAO members not enumerated/classified (insider vs non-insider) this run, so Security-Council qualification (>=50% non-insider, publicly announced) could not be confirmed; getMemberAt(uint256) per-index reads not performed.

C6: guardian 0x0cCF14983364A7735d369879603930Afe10df21e actor_class (EOA vs multisig) not classified on-chain this run; whether any residual guardian power reaches T1 with deployedStatus=true was not exhaustively traced.

C5: RocketDAOProtocol/RocketDAOProtocolProposal (pDAO, 0xCaC2.../0x2D62...) tokenholder-vote parameters (proposal threshold, quorum, voting period, execute delay on rocketDAOProtocolSettingsProposals 0xf6ad...) not read this run; pDAO governs parameters/treasury (T2) not code upgrades, but its timing/quorum were not verified.

admin_addresses.role: RocketDAONodeTrusted — Oracle DAO, 10 members, 51% quorum; authorizes upgrades
RocketStorage — registry; setAddress defines all contract implementations
RocketDAOProtocol — pDAO core (parameters/treasury, not code upgrades)

protocol_metadata.about: Rocket Pool is a decentralised Ethereum liquid staking protocol: users deposit ETH to mint the rETH liquid staking receipt, while node operators run minipools backed by RPL collateral. Contract logic is upgraded via a registry-pointer pattern (RocketStorage holds every contract's address), with code upgrades authorized by a 10-member Oracle DAO of trusted nodes and protocol parameters/treasury governed by a separate RPL tokenholder Protocol DAO.
